summary: Deimos is an AI-powered platform that identifies Earth locations with environmental and geological characteristics similar to selected locations on the Moon or Mars. By entering a planetary body and geographic coordinates, users can explore the five closest Earth analog locations through a multi-feature similarity model, helping researchers and mission planners better understand planetary environments using real-world comparisons
details:
Deimos System

Project Overview

Deimos System is a data-driven platform designed to identify locations on Earth that share similar environmental and geological characteristics with specific locations on the Moon and Mars.

Understanding extraterrestrial environments is essential for future space exploration, particularly when studying potential landing sites, surface conditions, and locations that could support scientific research or future human missions. However, interpreting planetary data can be challenging, especially when researchers need to relate unfamiliar extraterrestrial conditions to environments they can observe and study on Earth.

Our project addresses this challenge by transforming planetary coordinates into meaningful Earth-based comparisons.

How It Works

The platform provides a simple coordinate-based interface. Users select their target celestial body (Moon or Mars) and enter its latitude and longitude.

The system then:

  1. Retrieves the available environmental and geological features associated with the selected planetary location.
  2. Processes and compares these features with corresponding data from locations across Earth.
  3. Applies a trained Similarity Model to evaluate how closely Earth locations match the selected planetary environment.
  4. Ranks the results and identifies the Top 5 most similar Earth locations.

Instead of returning a single general comparison, the platform provides a ranked list of potential Earth analogs, supported by similarity scores and feature-level comparisons.

Data Sources

The system integrates +10 datasets and data products covering Earth, Mars, and the Moon, primarily sourced from NASA Earthdata and NASA's Planetary Data System (PDS).

These datasets provide complementary information across several environmental and geological dimensions:

  • Temperature: Surface and planetary thermal measurements.
  • Albedo and Reflectance: Information related to how surfaces reflect incoming solar radiation.
  • Elevation: Terrain elevation and surface topography.
  • Slope: The inclination of the terrain.
  • Roughness: Variations in surface topography.
  • Atmospheric Conditions: Available atmospheric measurements and environmental parameters.

Combining these data sources allows the system to move beyond single-variable comparisons and evaluate planetary environments through multiple features.

Similarity Model

At the core of the platform is a trained Similarity Model that compares the environmental and geological characteristics of a selected Moon or Mars location against Earth locations.

The model evaluates multiple features and produces a ranked set of the five closest Earth analogs.

The platform also aims to make the comparison interpretable by presenting feature-level information alongside the overall similarity results. This allows users to understand which characteristics contribute to the similarity between the selected planetary location and each recommended Earth location.

Expected Impact

Earth Analog Discovery System provides an accessible way to explore relationships between extraterrestrial environments and Earth's diverse landscapes.

Potential applications include:

  • Supporting preliminary research into planetary surface environments.
  • Identifying terrestrial locations that may serve as analog environments for scientific field studies.
  • Helping researchers and students explore planetary datasets through geographic comparisons.
  • Making complex NASA planetary and Earth observation data more accessible and understandable.

Limitations and Future Development

An Earth analog is not an exact physical replica of a lunar or Martian environment. Similarity in measured environmental and geological features does not imply identical conditions, particularly for factors such as gravity, radiation, atmospheric pressure, and other extraterrestrial characteristics.

Future development could incorporate additional datasets, improve spatial and temporal data alignment, expand the range of comparable planetary features, and introduce more advanced validation and visualization capabilities.

Ultimately, our goal is to make planetary environmental comparison more accessible: users provide one location on the Moon or Mars, and the system discovers five Earth locations with the closest measurable similarities.
